entry.title: Bike Lane Sweeper Richmond, September 27
entry.content:
From Bike Lane Sweeper Richmond



If you’ve signed up to be a zone captain, you’ll be responsible for storing the sweeper in your zone in between sweeps.

After the sweeper has been dropped off at your house, take a quick moment to inspect the sweeper to make sure the kickstand is down and the sweeper is not resting on the brush.

If the vest has been left out to dry, please hand wash it if needed.

Remove the rain cover, then remove the battery using the key and replace the rain cover until the battery is charged.

Take the battery inside to charge it using the charger. A red light means the battery is charging. A green light means the battery is charged.

Make sure the connector water gasket is closed after the battery is finished charging. Once the battery is charged, reinstall it on the sweeper, reinstall the rain cover, and put the vest away if it’s dry.

Check the indicator valve caps on the tires to see if the tires need to be pumped. If you see any yellow or red visible inside of the caps, please pump up the tires. There is a pump and tire gauge in the safety kit that you can use to get up the pressure.

Ensure the safety kit has been properly sealed so the contents won’t get wet.

Lock up the safety kit, the sweeper, and the lockbox using the U-lock and place the keys back in the lockbox.

Finally, fill out the form you received via text to let the next volunteer know the sweeper is ready.

entry.title: Bike Lane Sweeper Richmond, September 24
entry.content:
From Bike Lane Sweeper Richmond



When you arrive to pick up your sweeper, you’ll find the waterproof safety kit bag locked up with it.

The code to unlock the safety kit is the first three digits of the code you received via text.

In the back, you’ll find a helpful guide that explains what’s inside.

You should find the rain cover on the sweeper protecting the control box and the battery from heavy rains. There’s also a bag to store it in inside the kit while you’re sweeping or during transfers.

Volunteers should always wear one of the high-vis vests, and there are three sizes to choose from.

The sweeper remote from the attachments bag can be quickly attached to your bike. One press turns the sweeper brush on, another turns it off. If the remote is missing, let us know. You can still sweep using the manual on and off switch.

In the attachments bag, there’s a right side rear view mirror that can be handy for looking at the sweeper without having to turn around. It can be useful when sweeping next to curbs or to avoid clipping curbs while turning.

You should wear gloves whenever you handle the sweeper. There are two sizes of gloves to choose from. You can keep the gloves with you by clamping them to your handlebars.

Protect your nose and mouth from breathing in any dust with a KN95 respirator. If you take a KN95, it’s yours to keep. Please don’t put it back in the bag.

Protect your eyes from dust using the included pair of safety glasses.

There is a pump and tire gauge in the safety kit that you can use if the sweeper tires need air. There are also tire levers, a patch kit or wrench, and a spare tube in case your bike or the sweeper gets a flat.

If you want to take a video of the sweeper in action, there’s a phone mount that mounts well to a seat post or a rear rack. Use the wrench to make sure it’s nice and tight.

If you want to use pickup mode, you should put bags inside of the sweeper bins. There are heavy-duty trash bags in the safety kit. Grab at least two for each bin.

entry.title: Bike Lane Sweeper Richmond, September 23
entry.content:
From Bike Lane Sweeper Richmond



When the sweeper is in pickup mode, rather than debris being pushed into the gutter, it will bounce off the sweeper shield and back into the bins.

Because a full bin can weigh up to 70 pounds when full of common debris like sand, and we don’t want to just dump debris back into the street, to use pickup mode, you’ll need a bike that can tow heavy loads.

Electric bikes are great at providing assistance to be able to tow extra weight.

To switch into pickup mode, loosen the wing nuts on both sides and align the side that the battery is on with the stopper. the opposite side with its side shield and tighten both wing nuts.

If you want to use pickup mode, you should put bags inside of the sweeper bins. There are heavy-duty trash bags in the safety kit. Grab at least two for each bin.

If you have a standard electric bike, you’ll need to make runs to a trash can as soon as the bins are full. If you have an electric cargo bike, you may be able to carry some debris, reducing the number of runs you need to make to a trash can.

If you’re planning on carrying debris on your bike, you should bring five-gallon buckets to transfer full bags into to avoid a broken bag leaking into or onto your bike.

Make sure to check the weight limit on your cargo bike so you don’t overload it. If you’re new to pickup mode, you’ll want to check the weight of the bins regularly to ensure that they don’t get heavier than you’re able to lift.

Bins in pickup mode will fill up faster than you expect. I only swept a single pass on about 15 blocks before having to empty the bins.

When you’re ready to change out the bags, remove any sticks or long sharp objects that might pierce the bag before tying it shut. The bags will be hard to remove from the bins, so flip the bins over and lift the bin off the bag to remove it.

The trash bags we’re using are 42-gallon contractor bags cut in half. If you used the last trash bag, let us know in the drop-off form and we’ll take care of it for the next volunteer.

entry.title: Bike Lane Sweeper Richmond, September 22
entry.content:
From Bike Lane Sweeper Richmond



After you finish sweeping, return the sweeper to the pickup location.

Empty any debris that made it into the bins during push mode into a trash bag from the safety kit.

Make sure to wipe down your bike any attachments you used and any parts of the sweeper that regularly get handled.

Beat the gloves out and shake the vest out of any dust. Flip down the sweeper kickstand and put the sweeper back where you found it.

Cover the control box and the battery with the rain cover to keep them dry in case of heavy rain.

After removing the tow arm, place it back in the slot at the top of the sweeper.

Make sure to return any accessories you used to the safety kit. Then follow the instructions to reseal the bag to keep the contents dry.

Lock up the safety kit, the sweeper, and the lockbox using the U-lock and place the keys back in the lockbox.

If the safety vest you used is sweaty, please leave it draped over the safety kit to dry.

When you get home, wash your clothes and take a shower to wash off any dust you might have been exposed to.
